newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Govt adds 2,700/mth to Australia jobless - Oppn.
newsitem.headline: Govt adds 2,700/mth to Australia jobless - Oppn.

text.p: Australia's jobless had risen by 2,700 people per month over the year since the conservative government took office, Labor opposition employment spokesman Martin Ferguson said on Thursday.
"Every month John Howard has been prime minister, 2,700 have joined the ranks of the jobless," Ferguson said in a statement.
"Every month he has been prime minister, 500 Australians have lost full-time jobs," Ferguson said, commenting on the latest labour force data.
The Liberal-National coalition swept into power in March 1996 ending 13 years of labor rule and in its 1996/97 budget forecast annual jobs growth of 1.5 percent.
"Seventy seven thousand jobs need to be created each month if the Howard government is to meet its modest budget target of 1.5 percent jobs growth," Ferguson said.

The seasonally adjusted estimate of the number of unemployed persons fell 7,800 to 803,000 in March from the previous month, compared with 770,800 in March 1996, the statistics bureau said on Thursday.
In trend terms, the number of unemployed persons rose slowly over the past year, reaching 801,400 million in March.
